facts.claim: Major dietary transitions plausibly altered sleep duration, architecture, circadian timing, neuroendocrine regulation, and the temporal alignment between feeding behavior and biological rhythms.
facts.quote: how each major dietary transition plausibly altered sleep duration, architecture, circadian timing, neuroendocrine regulation, and the temporal alignment between feeding behavior and biological rhythms.

facts.claim: Metabolic health and sleep integrity depend on when food is consumed in relation to biological rhythms shaped over deep evolutionary time.
facts.quote: the emerging framework of "evolutionary chrononutrition" proposes that metabolic health and sleep integrity depend not only on what humans eat, but critically on when food is consumed in relation to endogenous circadian architecture shaped across deep evolutionary time.

facts.claim: Circadian rhythm misalignments caused by environmental factors like late-night work and skipping breakfast are linked to negative impacts on endocrine and reproductive functions.
facts.quote: Circadian rhythm misalignments due to environmental factors, including late-night work and skipping breakfast, negatively impact endocrine and reproductive functions.

research.verdict: The sources provide a framework for how environmental and dietary changes affect circadian rhythms and metabolic health but do not contain specific data on the steam engine or industrial timekeeping.
